title: Mirage: An RNS-Based Photonic Accelerator for DNN Training
problem: Photonic hardware for DNN training is limited by precision constraints from expensive data converters and analog noise, preventing accurate training of state-of-the-art networks despite photonic computing's success in inference applications.
motivation: Photonic computing enables highly efficient matrix multiplication, a fundamental operation in DNNs, offering exceptional energy efficiency compared to electronic accelerators.
method: Mirage uses Residue Number System (RNS), a modular arithmetic-based numeral system, to decompose high-precision DNN training operations into multiple low-precision modular operations implemented natively in the analog photonic domain. The system features a novel photonic tensor core micro-architecture and dataflow that performs modular arithmetic directly in analog, combining the precision guarantees of RNS with the energy efficiency of photonic hardware.
key_novelty: Applying Residue Number System (RNS) to photonic tensor cores, enabling high-precision DNN training by performing multiple low-precision modular arithmetic operations natively in the analog photonic domain.
contributions: Novel RNS-based photonic tensor core micro-architecture for high-precision analog computation
Demonstration of training state-of-the-art DNNs with accuracy comparable to FP32 on photonic accelerators
23.8x faster training and 32.1x lower EDP compared to systolic arrays in iso-energy scenarios
42.8x lower power consumption with comparable or better EDP in iso-area scenarios
primary_theme: Photonic accelerator for high-precision DNN training
